A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IAPL study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and references throughout. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; v1 refers to supplementary material that is not included.

before.justification: V1 reports original IAPL evaluations on UniversalFakeDetect and GenImage, component ablations, and feature and attention visualizations.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark evaluations and reports additional ablation results, parameter sweeps and comparative attention visualizations.

M1.justification: The documented pipeline retains MLP adapters, two conditional branches, gated prompt propagation, confidence-selected entropy minimization and highest-confidence view selection. Renaming shallow tokens as test-time adaptive tokens and reorganizing CDAP into token tuning and separate view selection do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions train on ProGAN for UniversalFakeDetect and SD v1.4 for GenImage, evaluating the same 19 and eight subsets respectively. The additional ablations and visual examples remain within existing coverage.

E2.justification: UniversalFakeDetect Tables 1-2 remove CNN-Spot, Patchfor and Co-occurence. GenImage Table 3 removes Spec, CNN-Spot, F3Net and GramNet. The remaining comparison methods, including the strongest reported competitors, are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds experiments varying N_t over 3, 6, 9 and 12 and tuning steps over 1, 2 and 3, plus separate real/fake accuracy reporting. The main benchmark protocols and default settings remain unchanged. N_t is inconsistently called a token count despite its earlier definition as a prompted-layer endpoint.

E4.justification: V2 adds N_t and tuning-step sensitivity studies and separates the gating contribution in its revised component ablation. Figure 5 replaces the cross-view Grad-CAM example with comparisons without and with IAPL. Adapter-placement and UniversalFakeDetect entropy-loss analyses are retained, while the GenImage entropy-loss ablation is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. Prediction-confidence selection is retained and does not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All shared entries in Tables 1-3 are unchanged, including IAPL's 95.61% UniversalFakeDetect mAcc, 99.32% mAP and 96.7% GenImage mAcc. V2 adds or replaces supporting results, including tuning-step accuracies of 94.47%, 94.88% and 94.94%, class-specific accuracies and new Grad-CAM findings. Removed comparator and GenImage loss-ablation entries also reduce reported results.

T1.justification: The confidence score, entropy objectives and additive gated prompt updates retain their mathematical substance, with reordered equations and consolidated notation. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The second introduction contribution shifts from introducing CIL and CDAP to an efficient adaptation scheme combining lightweight adapters and learnable tokens. The central image-adaptive generalization claim and headline state-of-the-art performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 interprets its new Grad-CAM comparison as improved attention to forgery-related regions versus irrelevant baseline attention; v1 emphasized semantic regions across different views. It also adds capacity/efficiency explanations for N_t selection and the effectiveness/efficiency tradeoff behind two tuning steps.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly documents the 1024-dimensional encoder features and channel-wise gating coefficients. Existing hardware, optimizer, training budget, token counts and test-time tuning defaults remain consistent. The code destination is unchanged, now presented through a hyperlink.

R1.justification: V2 adds related-work discussion and citations for LAA-Net and Effort, while removing references associated with Patchfor, Co-occurence and GramNet. These are limited updates; the overall positioning against static adaptation and existing prompt-learning methods remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Section 3 changes from training/testing organization to Overview, Fixed Learned Parameters, Image-Adaptive Prompt Learning and Optimal View Selection, with revised terminology and expanded explanations of parameter roles.

P2.justification: V2 adds a conceptual Figure 1, redraws the architecture diagrams, relocates the retained t-SNE visualization and replaces the Grad-CAM exhibit. Ablation tables are split and restructured, while captions, highlighting, typography and page layout are substantially reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies fixed versus adaptive parameter roles and adds useful component controls, class-specific results and sensitivity analyses supporting design choices. The main benchmark evidence remains unchanged, with strong comparators retained. Removing the GenImage entropy-loss check and introducing inconsistent N_t terminology and a stale entropy-table reference limit the gains, but the added analysis and clearer organization support a modest overall improvement.
